SESSION SUMMARY

Patient Symptoms: Mild upper-respiratory symptoms are most consistent with a common cold
Primary Differential: Common cold (high confidence). Secondary Consideration(s): Allergies or nasal irritation, Strep throat.
Further Investigations: Continue supportive care and monitor symptoms over the next several days.; Consider a COVID-19 test if you have had a possible exposure, if testing is available, or if symptoms change, since no respiratory-virus testing has been performed..

PATIENT SUMMARY

The patient has had a mild sore throat and runny nose or congestion continuously for about 3 days, with throat discomfort rated 3/10. The patient reports no fever, cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, headache, ear pain, body aches, difficulty swallowing, neck stiffness, or neck swelling. The patient has no significant medical history, take no regular medications, and have no known medication allergies. No physical examination, vital signs, laboratory results, or photo evidence are available, and recent sick-contact exposure was not clearly established.

Home care

Seek urgent medical care immediately for breathing difficulty, chest pain, inability to swallow fluids, drooling, rapidly worsening swelling, or confusion. Contact a clinician promptly if a fever develops, symptoms worsen substantially, or symptoms are not improving after about 7 to 10 days.
